scope.mutations: every diagrammatic Conway circle, three rotations: PD and braid-closure diagrams for at most 11 crossings, PD diagrams for 12-13 crossings; composites with crossing sum <= 9

Fillings actually built: |p| <= 30, q <= 4 for prime knots with at most 11 crossings; |p| <= 30, q <= 2 for 12 crossings; |p| <= 30, q = 1 for 13 crossings; torus slope set for torus knots; none for composites and cables (S3/S4 need no recognition)
scope.recognition time limit: 1.5 s per filling (at most 11 crossings), 0.3 s (12 crossings), 0.2 s (13 crossings), 0.5 s for torus-knot fillings (shrunk from 60 s); enforced inside the Regina retriangulation search instead of a subprocess; each node is processed by a worker that is replaced if it crashes or exceeds 25 minutes
scope.coincidence certificates: candidates are fillings with equal |p| and volume within 2e-7; verification (verify_hyperbolicity) and the verified isometry signature are computed only for candidates, in priority order (clusters containing a node with pinned r_2 or r_0 first) under a time budget; self-coincidences p/q, -p/q of amphichiral knots are skipped because their equations are implied by F5/C5
scope.peripheral nodes: a result that is not a core node is instantiated as a node only if it is reached from two distinct nodes or a homogeneous diagram of it was found; other identified results are counted (parameters.json, stats) but not instantiated; unidentified results are discarded. Census names (K14a.., K14n.., K15a.., K15n..) come from the SnapPy census of 14-15 crossing knots (300,265 knots, matched by orientation-sensitive verified isometry signature)
scope.calculator: KnotInfo PD codes of all table knots; construction diagrams of composites, torus knots and family constructions; cable diagrams with at most 40 crossings (10 s limit); every instantiated peripheral node known when the checkpoint started (60 s limit; 184,868 results, no failures); complexes (milestone 7) only for nodes whose upsilon was not pinned, and for peripheral nodes only if they are Floer-thin or carry the L-space flag (U2)
scope.identification: Regina solid-torus test only when the Alexander polynomial is trivial; Regina isosig matching of non-hyperbolic results against the pool of torus knots, composites, family constructions and small cables with a bounded retriangulation search
scope.rule instantiations for peripheral nodes: I1-I3 and the unary rules use the calculator output of the node (genus, fibredness, tau, epsilon, L-space flag, ranks). C8 and U2a are instantiated for census knots whose census name marks them as alternating (K14a.., K15a..), with tau from the calculator; C8 also for nodes with a homogeneous diagram found by a pass; U3 for nodes whose calculator epsilon is 0

Export layout and memory (2026-11-11): The export is packed: JSONL files are gzip parts of at most 40 MiB, chain files are members of chains/chains-NNN.tar.xz, knots.csv is continued in knots.N.csv, peripheral nodes are in knots_peripheral[.k].xlsx (FORMAT.md, "Parts and packing"). scripts/export_pack.py unpack restores the literal section-9 file names; the checker and route.py read both layouts.

No file exceeds 50 MB. Reference tables that grew past the limit (census signatures, calculator outputs of peripheral nodes) are stored as deduplicated parts under data/ref_census and data/hfk_peripheral.

Memory. With the calculator inputs of the peripheral nodes the problem outgrew the machine (16 GB): the solver needed 6.4 GB, the checker 9.6 GB, and a check-in solve was killed. Constraints, events and move edges are now stored as columns (objects are built when one is read), the node tables are written row by row, the ablation runs are separate processes started after the export, and the checker reads events.jsonl front to back with the constraints in a temporary file. The reworked code was run on a frozen copy of the input of the committed export: all 20 files of the solve and export are byte-identical, the 16 ablation runs give the same counts, and the reworked checker prints the same summary. Peak memory: solve and export 2.2 GB, checker 2.4 GB.

The rework does not touch operators, rule instantiation or the order of propagation: the work list is processed in the same order as before (fresh constraints in order, then re-queued ones first in, first out).
